subject: Post-demo: Atlas Health evaluation — ownership, success criteria, and runbook
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@atlashealth.com>, Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Atlas Health evaluation — ownership, success criteria, and runbook

Hi Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before we start the 30-day evaluation: 

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood’s hosted inference for patient-note summarization and triage routing, with an eye to production latency under 600ms p50 and consistent PHI handling.

Success criteria (what Atlas will measure)
- Accuracy: Clinician-rated summary quality >= 85% on our sample prompts
- Latency: 95th percentile per-request latency < 900ms for 1–2k concurrent users
- Cost: estimated per-visit token cost < $0.10 in steady state
- Security: SOC2-A evidence (see questionnaire) and isolation for PHI during transit

Proposed evaluation plan (week-by-week)
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff, access, security questionnaire 
- Week 1: Ingest sample dataset, baseline runs, latency profiling
- Week 2: Integration tests with your staging app + live traffic shadowing (non-PHI)
- Week 3: Small pilot with de-identified PHI subset if your team approves
- Week 4: Final metrics review and decision sync

Ownership / RACI (high level)
- Atlas Infra: Owner — Tom Garcia (responsible) — provide staging AWS account + network peering for shadowing
- Atlas App: Owner — Emily Chen (responsible) — integration, acceptance of summary quality
- Redwood Infra: Owner — Rishi Malhotra (responsible) — provisioning, model selection, latency tuning
- Redwood Security: Owner — Marissa Cole (accountable) — complete SOC2 questionnaire and provide audit logs
- Procurement / Legal: Atlas Procurement (consulted) + Redwood Sales (informed)

Immediate asks for this week
1) Emily/Tom: Please confirm a staging AWS role or temporary credentials we can use for the shadowing tests by EOD Thursday (2/12).
2) Tom: Can you confirm who on your side owns procurement/PO for potential pilot spend?
3) Emily: Share a representative sample of notes (de-identified) and the clinician scoring rubric.

Attachments: I attached the security questionnaire and a first-pass runbook (redwood-eval-runbook-v1.xlsx). I’ll circulate a brief MoA draft if we move to pilot.

I’ll loop back after I get the staging access details and will propose a kickoff calendar invite.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--

From: Emily Chen <emily@atlashealth.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Atlas Health evaluation — ownership, success criteria, and runbook

Thanks, Vanessa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the accuracy metric, our clinicians use a 1–5 rubric; I’ll convert to percentage for consistency. We can commit to scoring 50 samples in Week 2.
- Staging access: I can provision a cross-account role. Tom, do you want me to provision it or should our infra team (Sam) do it?
- Procurement: we have a small evaluation budget; PO would come from our Digital Trials line (I’ll confirm PO contact).

Two quick asks: 
1) Can Redwood provide a short checklist of required IAM policies and a minimal network diagram for peering?
2) Is a non-PHI shadowing run in Week 2 sufficient to validate latency and integration, or do you need de-identified samples earlier?

Emily
Emily Chen
Director, Clinical Informatics — Atlas Health
emily@atlashealth.com | +1 212-555-0987

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@atlashealth.com>, Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Atlas Health evaluation — ownership, success criteria, and runbook

Hi Emily — great questions, thanks. Short answers below and then an inline RACI table (compact) so everyone has a single source of truth.

- IAM & network: Attached is a one-page checklist and minimal VPC peering diagram. We only need a role with AssumeRole and S3 read permissions for the sample ingestion path; for shadowing we’ll use HTTPS to your staging endpoint (no inbound open ports).
- Shadowing vs de-identified PHI: Shadowing with non-PHI traffic will validate latency and integration. For clinician scoring we’ll need the de-identified set in Week 3 when you’re comfortable.

Inline RACI (concise):
- Provisioning staging role: R=Tom (Atlas Infra), A=Tom, C=Rishi, I=Vanessa
- Sample data supply: R=Emily (Atlas App), A=Emily, C=Marissa, I=Vanessa
- Security questionnaire completion: R=Marissa (Redwood Sec), A=Marissa, C=Emily, I=Vanessa
- Latency tuning & model config: R=Rishi (Redwood Infra), A=Rishi, C=Tom, I=Emily
- Procurement/PO: R=Atlas Procurement, A=Atlas Procurement, C=Vanessa

Next steps I’ll take this afternoon:
- Send the VPC/IAM checklist (attached)
- Create calendar invites for Week0 kickoff (30m) and Week2 integration test (1h)
- Drop a short spreadsheet column for each success criterion so we can track scores live

If that looks good I’ll book the kickoff for Thu 2/12 at 10am PT.

Cheers,
Vanessa

--

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Atlas Health evaluation — ownership, success criteria, and runbook

Quick infra note — tagging for clarity: I’ll take responsibility for provisioning the Redwood side and selecting the model variant for the eval. Two things Atlas should confirm ASAP:
1) Whether the staging role we’ll assume allows temporary STS tokens (preferred) or whether you need us to upload a public key for limited-access API calls. STS tokens make rotation during the eval much simpler.
2) Target concurrency for the shadowing test: Emily mentioned 1–2k users. Please confirm if that’s steady or a peak; I’ll size the test fleet accordingly.

I’ll also post logs for the Week 1 baseline run into the shared Drive folder and tag them with RDW-4381 so Marissa can attach them to the questionnaire.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
